outline.title: Abstract
outline.description: A concise summary of the survey's scope, covering the evolution of LLM security from 2023 to 2026. It highlights the transition from simple prompt exploits to complex architectural vulnerabilities, including data poisoning, adversarial attacks, hallucinations, and prompt injections. The abstract summarizes the shift toward agentic security and reasoning-based threats, concluding with the necessity for holistic defense frameworks.

outline.title: Introduction
outline.description: This section motivates the critical need for LLM security research, citing the rapid deployment of these models in sensitive domains. It outlines the scope of the survey (2023-2026), moving from foundational risks in code generation [Improta_2023_AI] to the sophisticated exploitation of autonomous agents and reasoning models [Cui_2025_LLM, Zhu_2025_Think]. It defines the survey's contributions, including a novel taxonomy of threats across the model lifecycle and a comprehensive analysis of testing methodologies.

outline.title: Background and Preliminaries
outline.description: Provides essential technical foundations for LLM security. It covers the transformer architecture, alignment processes like RLHF and DPO [Baumgartner_2024_RLHF], and the mechanics of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. This section establishes a formal threat model, defining attacker goals (e.g., integrity, confidentiality), capabilities (white-box vs. black-box), and the distinction between training-time and inference-time interventions.

outline.title: Data and Model Poisoning: Training-Time Vulnerabilities
outline.description: Analyzes the fragility of the LLM supply chain. It begins with early work on targeted data poisoning in code generators [Improta_2023_AI] and the manipulation of preference datasets in RLHF/DPO via label-flipping [Baumgartner_2024_RLHF, Kusaka_2025_LLM]. The section explores the 2025 shift toward 'behavioral' and 'reasoning' poisoning, where attackers target the internal logic of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) to induce deceptive reasoning [Zhu_2025_Think, Shen_2025_Decepchain]. It also covers multilingual backdoor transfers [He_2024_LLMs] and domain-specific poisoning in code [Yan_2024_LLM, Hossen_2024_Double].

outline.title: Adversarial Attacks: Exploiting Model Mechanics
outline.description: Examines the evolution of adversarial exploits from 2023 to 2026. It details the transition from simple prompt-based exploits to deep architectural vulnerabilities. Key topics include white-box analysis tools for measuring backdoor triggers in neuron activations [Cheng_2024_Unit, Hussain_2024_Measuring], multi-turn conversational exploits [Hao_2024_Exploring], and 'context-shifting' strategies that bypass guardrails [Noever_2024_AI]. The section highlights the 2025 shift toward attacking autonomous agents, specifically control-flow hijacking in the ReAct framework and the weaponization of agents for CVE exploitation.

outline.title: Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking: From Chatbots to Agents
outline.description: Focuses on the manipulation of model instructions. It reviews structural and formatting vulnerabilities such as 'FlipAttack' [Liu_2024_Flipattack] and 'AutoDan' [Liu_2024_Autodan]. A major focus is the 2025 paradigm shift toward Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) in multi-modal and autonomous systems, including web navigation and coding editors [Shi_2025_LLM, Wang_2025_Webinject, Johnson_2025_LLM]. The section also analyzes vulnerabilities unique to Reasoning LLMs (RLLMs) like DeepSeek-R1, where internal CoT processes are exploited [Cui_2025_LLM, Cui_2025_LLMs].

outline.title: Hallucinations and Factual Integrity
outline.description: Addresses the security implications of non-factual generations. It explores the 'language prior' problem in Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where models ignore visual input [Wang_2024_Mllm, Xing_2024_Mitigating]. The section details the use of Natural Language Inference (NLI) for factual consistency [Jing_2024_Scale, Zhang_2024_Comparative] and the 2025 trend of using specialized small-scale models (e.g., Paladin) to outperform proprietary models in hallucination detection [Ivry_2025_Paladin, Yaron_2025_GPT]. Domain-specific grounding in climate science [Thulke_2025_Listen] and healthcare is also discussed.

outline.title: Cross-Cutting Defenses and Mitigation Strategies
outline.description: Synthesizes defense mechanisms across all threat categories. It covers internal activation monitoring to detect backdoors [Cheng_2024_Unit], robust alignment techniques to counter poisoning [Baumgartner_2024_RLHF], and the use of specialized small models for real-time hallucination and injection filtering [Ivry_2025_Paladin]. The section also discusses the evolution of guardrails from simple prompt engineering to internal state auditing and the development of 'immune' agentic frameworks.

outline.title: Testing Methodologies and Evaluation
outline.description: A mandatory section synthesizing how LLM security is measured. It covers benchmarks for adversarial robustness (e.g., AdvBench), factual consistency (NLI-based), and poisoning (label-flipping metrics). It highlights specialized evaluation frameworks like RMCBench [Chen_2024_Rmcbench] and tools for white-box auditing [Cheng_2024_Unit]. The section discusses metrics such as Attack Success Rate (ASR), perplexity-based detection, and the use of 'LLM-as-a-judge' for evaluating complex reasoning and agentic safety [Paudel_2025_Hallucinot].

outline.title: Discussion and Open Challenges
outline.description: Identifies critical gaps in current research. It discusses the 'cat-and-mouse' game between automated attack generation and alignment, the difficulty of securing long-context reasoning processes, and the emerging threats in the model supply chain. It highlights the challenge of balancing model utility with safety, particularly in specialized domains like code generation and healthcare, and the need for standardized, cross-lingual security benchmarks.

outline.title: Conclusion
outline.description: Summarizes the key findings of the survey, emphasizing the transition of LLM security from a niche concern to a foundational requirement for autonomous systems. It provides practical recommendations for researchers and practitioners, advocating for a multi-layered defense-in-depth approach that spans the entire model lifecycle from data curation to inference-time monitoring.
